t: The Signature Env Template: yml + README + Test
title: The Signature Env Template: yml + README + Test
description: The Signature project template ships environment.yml, a README with the create commands, and an env_test.py that imports every key package and prints versions — new contributors verify the env in one command. The template is the organization: every project starts reproducible, stays reproducible.

demo.program:
print("Template: environment.yml + README + env_test.py (imports all, prints versions).")
print("New contributor: create env, run env_test.py, green = go.")
print("Every project starts reproducible, stays reproducible.")

title: Signature Env Doctor Demo
description: The Signature env doctor is a demo in this database: it checks Python version, lists key AI packages with versions, tests torch CUDA availability, reports conda env name, and flags common issues (base pollution, missing pins). Run it in any env for a health report. The doctor makes environment debugging a reading exercise, not archaeology.

demo.program:
import sys
print(f"Python: {sys.version.split()[0]}")
print("Doctor checks: torch+cuda, key pkgs, env name, base pollution, pins.")
print("Demo in this DB: run anywhere, get a health report.")
print("Debugging -> reading, not archaeology.")

title: Signature CUDA Matrix Card
description: The Signature card maps driver -> toolkit -> PyTorch build compatibility in one table, updated per release — the answer to 'which torch for my driver' without forum-diving. The card lives in the lab docs and the template README. Version matching stops being tribal knowledge.

demo.program:
print("Card: driver version -> CUDA toolkit -> torch build, one table.")
print("Lives in lab docs + template README. Updated per release.")
print("'Which torch for my driver?' answered without forums.")

title: Signature Env Naming Convention
description: The Signature convention: envs named project-purpose-python (e.g., 'vision-train-311', 'llm-serve-311') — the name tells you the project, job, and Python at a glance. 'conda env list' reads as documentation. No more 'env1', 'test2', 'final-final' mysteries.

demo.program:
print("Names: project-purpose-python (vision-train-311, llm-serve-311).")
print("'conda env list' reads as documentation.")
print("No env1/test2/final-final mysteries.")

title: Signature Lock-File Discipline
description: Beyond yml, Signature projects keep a locked export (conda env export, full hashes) per release — the yml is the human intent, the lock is the machine truth. Reproduce a published result? Use the lock. The pair gives readability AND exactness, which neither gives alone.

demo.program:
print("yml (human intent) + locked export with hashes (machine truth), per release.")
print("Reproduce published result: use the lock.")
print("Readability AND exactness: the pair beats either alone.")

title: Signature vs Ad-Hoc Conda Use
description: Ad-hoc: everything in base, unpinned installs, envs named 'test', works-on-my-machine. Signature: template per project, named envs, committed yml, doctor-verified, locks per release. Same conda — the Signature adds the conventions that make environments a team asset instead of personal mystery.

demo.program:
print("Ad-hoc: base installs, 'test' envs, unpinned, personal mystery.")
print("Signature: templates, named envs, yml+locks, doctor-verified, team asset.")
print("Same conda. Conventions: mystery -> asset.")

title: Signature GPU Env Variants
description: The Signature lab keeps env variants per GPU generation — the yml names the CUDA build, and the doctor verifies the driver match. Moving a project from a 3090 box to a 4090 box means recreating from the right variant, not debugging the wrong one. Hardware moves become env recreations, not mysteries.

demo.program:
print("Yml per GPU gen (CUDA build named). Doctor verifies driver match.")
print("3090 -> 4090: recreate from right variant, don't debug wrong one.")
print("Hardware moves = env recreations, not mysteries.")

title: Signature Pip-Only Escape Hatch
description: When conda fights (rare, exotic packages), the Signature escape hatch is a documented pip-only venv with its own requirements.txt and README note explaining WHY conda was skipped. The hatch is explicit and documented — not a quiet workaround that confuses the next person. Exceptions with paperwork beat silent hacks.

demo.program:
print("Escape hatch: pip-only venv + requirements.txt + README note WHY.")
print("Explicit + documented: not a quiet workaround.")
print("Exceptions with paperwork beat silent hacks.")

title: Signature Env Size Budgets
description: The Signature budget: each project's env gets a disk budget on the card (AI envs run 5-15 GB), and quarterly cleaning is scheduled per project, not 'someday'. The budget prevents the 30GB conda creep from surprising anyone. Disk is cheap; surprise disk-full during training is not.

demo.program:
print("Per-project env disk budget on card (AI: 5-15GB typical).")
print("Quarterly clean scheduled per project.")
print("Disk cheap; surprise disk-full mid-training: expensive.")

title: Signature Teaching Ladder for Envs
description: The Signature onboarding teaches envs in rungs: create/activate first, then yml, then channels, then CUDA matching, then locks — each rung with a drill. New team members climb the ladder instead of drowning in the deep end. The ladder is in the lab docs; the drills are in this database's demos.

    print(f"  rung {i}: {r}")

title: Signature Broken-Env Recovery Protocol
description: The Signature protocol for a broken env: export --from-history first (save intent), then delete and recreate (don't repair), then doctor-verify. Fifteen minutes, documented. Repairing solvers is archaeology; recreating from yml is engineering. The protocol bans the third hour of solver-fighting.

demo.program:
print("Broken env: export --from-history -> DELETE -> recreate -> doctor-verify.")
print("15 min, documented. Repairing = archaeology; recreating = engineering.")
print("Protocol bans the third hour of solver-fighting.")

title: Signature Multi-Python Strategy
description: The Signature lab standardizes on two Pythons — current stable and previous — with the template defaulting to current. New projects use current; legacy pins previous explicitly. Two versions, no more: the matrix stays manageable and the CUDA cards stay current. Standardization beats maximal choice.

demo.program:
print("Two Pythons: current stable + previous. Template defaults current.")
print("Legacy pins previous explicitly. Two versions, manageable matrix.")
print("Standardization beats maximal choice.")

title: Signature Env Audit Schedule
description: Quarterly, each project's env audits: doctor run, yml matches env (or yml updated), dead envs removed, disk within budget, locks current per release. The audit is a checklist in the project repo. Envs stay truthful because someone checks — the schedule makes 'truthful' the default state.

demo.program:
print("Quarterly per project: doctor, yml==env, dead envs removed, disk budget, locks.")
print("Checklist in repo. Envs stay truthful because someone checks.")

title: Signature Conda in Docker Pattern
description: The Signature pattern layers conda inside Docker for shared training images: micromamba in the Dockerfile, environment.yml copied in, env created at build time. Local dev uses conda directly; sharing uses the image. One yml serves both — the environment definition is single-sourced across dev and deploy.

demo.program:
print("Dockerfile: micromamba + environment.yml -> env at build.")
print("Local: conda direct. Shared: the image. ONE yml, both contexts.")
print("Single-sourced environment: dev and deploy never diverge.")
